title: GPS time
summary: Time from a GPS receiver on USB or the UART, with no internet and no clock module: gpsd and chrony's reference clock.
consent: gpsd listens on the box for the receiver and answers programs on the box only. The receiver's position is kept by gpsd while it runs; nothing leaves the box.
notes: A box with no clock module boots hours behind (the clock doctor says so). A receiver with a fix gives chrony the time to the second; with its PPS pin wired to a GPIO, to the microsecond (pps-tools shows the pulses).

chrony's refclock lines (SHM from gpsd, PPS from /dev/pps0) go in /etc/chrony/conf.d; chrony then also serves time to the hotspot (allow 192.168.4.0/24), so guests' phones agree with the box's certificate dates.
gpsd is left running while the kit is installed; it starts when the receiver appears.
